context: An internal engineering meeting at Kestrel Health, a patient appointment-reminder platform, held two days after a notification pipeline outage on September 8th. The first part is a mini post-incident review; the rest debates keeping RabbitMQ versus migrating to Kafka (MSK) or SQS/SNS, plus outbox, idempotency, DLQ, autoscaling and alerting fixes, with the engineering director joining late to make the final call.

facts.statement: The notification pipeline outage under review happened on Tuesday, September 8th.
At 14:02 notif-worker version 2.14.0 (the RabbitMQ consumer that sends SMS via Twilio and email via SendGrid) was deployed.
notif-worker is the consumer service; notify-gateway is the HTTP service clinics call that publishes onto the queue.
The first alert fired at 14:19: the queue depth alert on notifications.v2 when depth crossed 50,000 messages.
Pam declared a SEV-2 at 14:31; it was upgraded to SEV-1 at 15:10 as depth passed 400,000 and clinics called customer success.
At 14:45 Sam rolled notif-worker back to 2.13.2, and the rollback did not help.
The backlog peaked at 1.8 million messages at 16:40.
At 16:52 Sam manually flipped RETRY_MODE back to delayed, which stopped the bleeding; the backlog drained by 18:35 and the incident was resolved at 19:12.
The incident lasted 4 hours and 53 minutes, from first alert at 14:19 to resolution at 19:12.
p99 end-to-end delivery latency was 2.1 seconds before the incident and reached 47 minutes at the worst point.
After the fix p99 delivery latency is 3.4 seconds, still above the 2.1 second baseline.
The Twilio 429 (rate-limited) rate went from a baseline of about 0.2% of sends to 38% at peak.
The overall notification failure rate (not delivered within the reminder window) was 11% for the incident window.
420 clinics were affected by the outage (per delivery logs, confirmed by customer success).
About 61,000 patients received late reminders and 9,400 patients received duplicate SMS messages.
notif-worker 2.14.0 raised RabbitMQ prefetch from 10 to 200, causing OOM kills (Pam counted 212 OOM kills between 14:20 and 16:50) - an amplifier, not the root cause.

The dead-letter queue was never enabled on notifications.v2: the Terraform policy pattern used a hyphen (notifications-v2) instead of a dot, so failed messages requeued forever and the DLQ has always had zero messages.
notif-worker is not on the Argo Rollouts canary pipeline (only notify-gateway and the scheduler are); it deploys straight to all replicas.
Refined root cause: the RETRY_MODE=inline ConfigMap change shipped with 2.14.0 made every retryable provider error an immediate nack/requeue with no backoff, creating a retry storm against Twilio.
The rollback did not help because the Helm rollback only rolled back the image; the ConfigMap lives in a separate chart, so 2.13.2 also ran with RETRY_MODE inline.
The trigger was a 240,000-reminder bulk batch uploaded by Northgate Medical Group through notify-gateway at 14:00.
KEDA scaled notif-worker on queue depth from 8 to 40 pods (max replicas 40), producing about 240 attempted sends per second against Twilio's 100 messages/second short code limit.
The duplicates came mainly from pods being OOM killed after Twilio accepted a message but before the RabbitMQ ack; there is no idempotency check on the send side.
About 2,300 notifications were never sent: notify-gateway wrote them to Postgres but publisher confirms timed out (after 5 seconds) and they were never published (dual-write problem).
Code freeze for peak season is October 23rd; open enrollment starts November 1st and notification volume roughly triples through mid December.
Current volume is about 3 million messages a day (~90 million a month), about 9 million a day at peak.
The platform team is four engineers (Dana, Ravi, Sam, and Joaquin, who is on parental leave until September 21st); Pam is an SRE shared across three teams at about half time.
The RabbitMQ cluster costs about $3,800 a month; the messaging budget ceiling is $6,000 a month, and Grace cannot raise it before the next fiscal year starting in February.
HIPAA: payloads contain PHI, so any service must be covered by the AWS BAA, encrypted at rest with customer managed KMS keys, and PHI may not sit in a broker longer than 14 days.
An auditor finding from March (RabbitMQ inter-node traffic not using TLS) is still open with an end-of-year due date.
Ravi advocated migrating to Kafka 3.6 on Amazon MSK before peak, citing replay, consumer-lag backpressure and per-clinic ordering.
Ravi's Kafka case drew on a QCon San Francisco talk from a food delivery company that had a similar retry-storm outage.
MSK would cost about $5,200 a month steady state (three kafka.m5.xlarge brokers incl. cross-AZ transfer, modelled on the data team's bill), and about $9,000 a month while dual-running with RabbitMQ.
Sam estimated the Kafka migration at 10 to 12 weeks for two people (quiet hours logic, retry topics), which would miss the October 23rd freeze.
Kafka would not by itself fix the retry storm, missing DLQ or autoscaling problem; Ravi conceded the retry storm is a consumer design problem, not a broker problem.
Pam estimated SQS plus SNS at $600-$1,100 a month (using $1,100), about $2,500 in 3x peak months, with built-in redrive DLQ, visibility-timeout backoff, BAA coverage and KMS CMK support.
SQS caveats: 256 KB message size limit (insurance card email payloads may be large), standard queues are unordered and at-least-once, and there is no replay.
Option one (stay on RabbitMQ): upgrade 3.11.9 to 3.13.7, move notifications.v2 from classic mirrored to quorum queues, costing about $4,300 a month and about three weeks of work.
notify-gateway will adopt the transactional outbox pattern: an outbox row in the same Postgres 14 transaction plus a relay running as its own deployment with its own alert.
Idempotency will use a Postgres delivery_attempts table with a unique index on notification ID plus channel, not Redis.
facts.notes: supersedes Sam's Redis SETNX 24h TTL idea (C05)

facts.statement: notif-worker max replicas will be capped at 16 (16 x 6 concurrent sends = 96/s, under Twilio's 100/s), down from 40, with a per-provider token bucket rate limiter and scaling on oldest message age instead of depth.
p99 is still 3.4 seconds (vs the 2.1 second baseline) because 2.14.1, rolled out Wednesday, still runs prefetch 200 with a raised memory limit; Sam expects dropping prefetch to 30 to recover it.

New alerts: page when oldest message age on notifications.v2 exceeds 180 seconds for 5 minutes; page when Twilio 429 rate exceeds 2% for 5 minutes; ticket when the DLQ has any message; page when the DLQ exceeds 500 messages.
facts.notes: age threshold supersedes 120 seconds (C07); replaces the 50,000 depth page

facts.statement: Final decision (made by Grace, confirmed by Dana): stay on RabbitMQ for peak season with the 3.13 upgrade, quorum queues and consumer fixes.
facts.notes: implicit supersession of the midpoint tentative Kafka direction (C08)

facts.statement: Kafka on MSK is rejected, not before peak and not on the post-peak roadmap unless something changes: $5,200 steady/$9,000 dual-run exceed the $6,000 ceiling, 10-12 weeks misses the freeze, it does not address the root cause, and the team lacks Kafka operations experience.
SQS/SNS gets a timeboxed prototype now, with the migration decision at the January 13th architecture review.
Sam deletes the inline retry mode and implements exponential backoff on the delayed exchange (1s, 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m, max five attempts, then dead letter) plus a Twilio token bucket limiter at 100/s.
Sam fixes the DLQ policy pattern in Terraform so notifications.v2 actually dead-letters.
Sam builds the delivery_attempts idempotency table with the unique index.
Pam owns the RabbitMQ 3.11.9 to 3.13.7 upgrade and migration of notifications.v2 to quorum queues with a delivery limit of 5 (reassigned from Ravi).
Dana owns the notification backlog runbook (config drift, DLQ checks, manual replica caps, pausing big batches; first section: rollback must include the ConfigMap chart), taken over from Pam.
Pam implements the new alerts and switches autoscaling to oldest message age.
Pam lowers notif-worker max replicas from 40 to 16 today.
Pam produces a 12-month cost estimate for all three options, including peak months and SQS dual-run, for Grace's early-October budget review.
Ravi runs the SQS/SNS prototype, timeboxed to 5 working days: notif-worker SMS path only, redrive policy, visibility timeout backoff, KMS CMK, and a check of largest payloads against 256 KB.
facts.deadline: start Monday, September 28th; readout Friday, October 2nd
facts.notes: replaces the two-week Kafka spike plan (C11)

facts.statement: Ravi moves notif-worker onto the Argo Rollouts canary pipeline.
Joaquin (back from leave September 21st) implements the outbox pattern and relay in notify-gateway; Dana briefs him on his first day.
Dana writes the architecture decision record.
Grace sends the incident note to the 420 clinics through customer success.
Sam drops notif-worker prefetch to 30 in a separate deploy.
Sales has promised two big hospital groups that reminders will be "bulletproof" for open enrollment.
There is a long-standing reschedule-then-cancel race condition; Pam suggested fixing it with a version number on the appointment rather than via queue ordering.
notif-worker includes quiet hours logic (no texts between 9pm and 8am local time) implemented by republishing to a delayed exchange with a TTL.
The nightly 02:00 batch for next-day appointments routinely pushes oldest message age to about 150 seconds.
Unresolved whether to resend or otherwise contact patients for the ~2,300 never-sent notifications; Grace has no answer yet.
Unresolved whether Twilio's 100 messages/second is a hard short-code limit or per account, and whether it can be raised for peak (no owner).
Unknown whether any insurance card email payloads exceed the 256 KB SQS limit.
Unknown whether the quorum queue migration needs a maintenance window (the 3.11 upgrade took a 20 minute window at 03:00).
Undecided whether email and SMS should be split into separate notif-worker deployments.

corrections.initial_value: prefetch bump 10->200 causing OOM kills plus Twilio rate limiting
corrections.final_value: RETRY_MODE=inline ConfigMap change causing no-backoff requeue retry storm (prefetch/OOM only an amplifier)
Postgres delivery_attempts unique index on notification ID plus channel

corrections.initial_value: tentatively migrate to Kafka on MSK before the October 23rd freeze
corrections.final_value: stay on RabbitMQ for peak with fixes; Kafka rejected; SQS prototype and January 13th decision

corrections.what: Owner of RabbitMQ 3.13.7 upgrade / quorum queue migration

corrections.initial_value: two-week Kafka consumer spike (plan by Monday) owned by Ravi

not_decisions.statement: Migrating the notification pipeline to Kafka on MSK (floated as the tentative direction at the midpoint, then rejected)
A two-week Kafka consumer spike plan by Ravi (cancelled)
Migrating to SQS/SNS - only a prototype was approved; the migration decision is deferred to January 13th
Using Redis SETNX with a 24 hour TTL for idempotency (rejected in favour of Postgres)
Throttling large per-clinic uploads at notify-gateway (floated, no owner, no decision)
Asking Twilio to raise short code throughput for peak (vague suggestion, no owner)
Running a game day on the pipeline (suggested by Grace, explicitly not assigned)
Splitting email and SMS into separate notif-worker deployments (said "ideally", not decided)

distractors.statement: Ravi assumed the dead-letter queue was enabled and poison messages were in notifications.v2.dlq
Pam assumed 2.14.0 had gone through canary so it probably was not the deploy
Initial theory that the prefetch change and OOM kills were the root cause
MSK at $1,900 a month and six-week migration
Small talk about Sam sleeping eleven hours and Ravi's kid asking if dinosaurs had birthdays
Tangent about the QCon San Francisco Kafka talk (neon green slides, "the log is the database", hand-drawn feature flag slides)
Joke that the autoscaler DDoSed their own vendor / t-shirt
Joke about which incident holds the worst-of-the-year trophy (April SSO incident)
Joke about putting the Kafka dream in the dead letter queue
Similar names: notif-worker (consumer) vs notify-gateway (publisher); Sam vs Pam
Old alert: page at queue depth 50,000 (being replaced)
Grace initially thought the meeting started at 3:30

open_questions_at_end: Whether to resend or otherwise contact patients for the ~2,300 never-sent notifications
Whether Twilio's 100 messages/second is a hard short-code or per-account limit and whether it can be raised for peak
Whether any insurance card email payloads exceed the 256 KB SQS limit
Whether the quorum queue migration needs a maintenance window
Whether to throttle large per-clinic uploads at notify-gateway (no owner; product input needed)
Whether to split email and SMS into separate notif-worker deployments
summary_must_include: Outage on September 8th: 4h53m, backlog peaked at 1.8M, p99 2.1s to 47 min (F01, F09, F07, F10)
Impact: 420 clinics, ~61,000 late reminders, 9,400 duplicate SMS, ~2,300 never sent (F14, F15, F24)
Root cause refined: RETRY_MODE=inline no-backoff retry storm, not prefetch/OOM; triggered by Northgate 240k batch (F19, F21)
DLQ was never enabled on notifications.v2 (F17)
Decision: stay on RabbitMQ for peak (3.13.7 + quorum queues + consumer fixes), ratified by Grace (F44)
Kafka/MSK rejected: cost over $6,000 ceiling, misses October 23rd freeze, does not fix root cause (F45, F28, F25)
SQS/SNS 5-day prototype by Ravi (readout October 2nd), decision January 13th (F55, F46)
Idempotency via Postgres unique index; outbox pattern in notify-gateway by Joaquin (F40, F57)
Max replicas capped at 16; alerts: oldest message age >180s, 429 rate >2%, DLQ thresholds (F41, F43)
Owner changes: Pam takes RabbitMQ upgrade (Oct 9th), Dana takes runbook (Sep 24th) (F50, F51)
Sam: backoff + rate limiter by September 25th (F47)
